Header: Cercospora coffeicola Brown eye spot, Berry blotch

Prevention: Brown-eye spot is a fungal disease that spreads by wind and rain splash, favoured by humid-warm conditions:
Too much shade, and poor air flow in the plantation favours the disease.
Plant healthy coffee seedlings with no diseased parts from a
In the nursery, provide 50% shade and aeration.
Arrange the plantings so that air moves between the rows and leaves.
Grow coffee at spacing of 10ft x 10ft (Robusta) and 8ft x 8ft (arabica) and provide (35-65%) shade.
You may intercrop coffee with banana as a temporary shade spaced at 20ft x20ft, or
Erythrina abyssinica are spaced at 45ft x 45ft.
Prune the coffee bushes to allow good aeration.
Do soil analysis and ensure that the soil has sufficient nitrogen and potassium.
Nitrogen and potassium deficiency increase the susceptibility of the plants.
Prune coffee adequately and cultivate with some shade to avoid any stress such as overbearing or sun-scorch that can make the berries particularly susceptible.
Monitoring: Inspect the plantation and the nursery once a week during warm humid conditions and once in 2 weeks during dry season.
Look for small pale yellow-white circular or angular spots on upper leaf surface.
Spots enlrage to become reddish-brown (5-15mm) with greyish centre.
Leaf spots may be surrounded by a yellow border.
Look for small raised red spots (red blister) on green or ripening berries.
Look for reddish dark brown patchy lesions on the berries (berry blotch) similar to those of coffee berry disease but not sunken.
Take action immediately in the nursery, when you see small pale yellow-white spots on upper leaf surface with a grey centre on leaves.
In the nursery, when leaves fall and stem of the seedling dies back, this is too late to take any control measures.
In the plantation, consider action when 50-80% of leaves on coffee trees are infected.
Direct Control: In the nursery, immediately remove and burn all seedlings having brown spots with gray centres to control the disease spread.
NPK fertilizer 500g per tree per season (250g per season) below the affected tree to increase its tolerance to the disease.
Remove infected twigs branches and berries and burn away from the field because they are a source of infection.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.
Always refer to the updated pesticide list by the
There is no synthetic fungicide that can cure an infected tree.
There are only protective contact fungicides that may prevent uninfected trees to become infected.
Foliar sprays with thorough coverage of leaves is required.
Interval (PHI): 14 days; Restricted re- entry interval (REI): 6 hours.
Copper sprays may kill insects that give biological control to the green scale insects.
Oxychloride such as 50% WP and others.
Multi-site action, Protective fungicide, FRAC M1 (inorganic).
